title: Influence of simulated temperature on the perception and Sensory function of the hand in virtual environments to reduce pain in traumatic hand injuries, neuropathy and CRPS (Complex Regional Pain Syndrome)
summary:
At the BG Clinic Tübingen, a new research project is underway, focusing on how advanced virtual technologies might aid in the recovery of hand function and deepen our understanding of various hand pathologies. This project stands out as it doesn’t center on direct therapeutic treatments but rather delves into fundamental research. The primary goal is to explore the potential of virtual environments in altering hand sensations and perceptions.

In recent years, the use of VR and AR in healthcare has significantly increased, offering immersive experiences that can impact multiple senses. These technologies have shown promise in various medical applications, but the underlying mechanisms, especially regarding their effects on pain perception in patients with hand injuries or conditions, are not fully understood. Our study seeks to bridge this knowledge gap.

The research involves both healthy individuals and patients with conditions like neuropathic pain, Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), and traumatic hand injuries. Neuropathic pain, caused by nerve damage or malfunction, manifests in various forms such as burning, tingling, and electric shock-like sensations, often leading to chronic discomfort. The study will utilize Extended Reality (XR) – a combination of VR and AR – to simulate sensations like heat or cold on participants' bodies. This innovative approach aims to study how these induced sensations affect cognitive perception and pain thresholds.

In addition to gathering feedback from participants about their experiences (using patient-reported outcome measures), the study will also collect objective data like skin conductance or heart rate. These measurements will provide a comprehensive view of the effects of virtual environments on sensory perception and pain management. This project could pave the way for new, more effective methods in treating hand-related pain conditions and improving patients' quality of life.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- subjects with healthy eyes or with corrected defective vision (glasses, contact lenses)
- existing CRPS diagnosis, neuropathy or existing traumatic hand injury
Exclusion criteria:
- Hearing impairment
- neuromuscular restrictions affecting the motor skills and sensitivity of the hands
- Amputation of more than 2 fingers (incl. thumb) per hand
- Insufficient knowledge of German
